cards.term: "The lunatic, the lover, and the poet, / Are of imagination all compact."
cards.def: Theseus says this in 5.1.8-10, grouping those three as people whose "shaping fantasies" outrun "cool reason."

cards.term: "gives to airy nothing / A local habitation and a name"
cards.def: Theseus says this of the poet's pen in 5.1.17-19, describing how imagination turns unknown forms into shapes, places, and people.

cards.term: "How easy is a bush suppos'd a bear!"
cards.def: Theseus says this in 5.1.23-24 as an everyday example of how "strong imagination" can turn a night-time fear into a supposed beast.
Hippolyta says this in 5.1.25-28, arguing that the lovers' shared, consistent story of the night "more witnesseth than fancy's images."

cards.term: "A tedious brief scene of young Pyramus / And his love Thisbe; very tragical mirth."
cards.def: Theseus reads this from Philostrate's paper in 5.1.61-63, then wonders at the oxymorons "merry and tragical" and "tedious and brief."

cards.term: "never anything can be amiss, / When simpleness and duty tender it."
cards.def: Theseus says this in 5.1.88-90 when he overrules Philostrate and agrees to hear the hard-handed men's play.

cards.term: "This fellow doth not stand upon points."
cards.def: Theseus says this in 5.1.128 after Quince's prologue, meaning the speaker misuses punctuation and pauses in the wrong places.

cards.term: "The best in this kind are but shadows, and the worst are no worse, if imagination amend them."
cards.def: Theseus tells Hippolyta this in 5.1.209-210 after she calls the play "the silliest stuff that ever I heard."

cards.term: "I, one Snug the joiner, am / A lion-fell, nor else no lion's dam."
cards.def: Snug, playing Lion, says this in 5.1.218-219 so the ladies will not fear he is a real lion.

cards.term: "This is old Ninny's tomb. Where is my love?"
cards.def: Thisbe (Flute) says this in 5.1.240, repeating the mechanicals' habitual mix-up of Ninus with "Ninny."
Bottom, as Pyramus, says this in 5.1.282 as he stabs himself, after which Demetrius puns that he is "no die, but an ace."
Theseus says this in 5.1.320-323 after refusing Bottom's offered epilogue and asking instead for a Bergomask dance.
Theseus says this in 5.1.323 when midnight has "told twelve," sending the lovers to bed and opening the way for the fairies' blessing.

cards.term: "If we shadows have offended, / Think but this, and all is mended, / That you have but slumber'd here."
cards.def: Puck says this in 5.2.56-59, asking the audience to take the play as a dream and, if they are friends, to give him their hands.
